artworks.title: Girl Horse

artist.name: Oksana Rubio
artist.bio: Oksana Rubio is originally from Ukraine and teaches art at the Tidewater Ukrainian School in Virginia Beach. She enjoys working in the mediums of wood, paint, bas-relief, and textiles. Using her many talents, Oksana specializes in breathing fresh life into her art and furniture. Oksana is able to source unique items for Ancestral Energy through her many connections of friends and family around the globe. She currently lives in Suffolk with her husband and step-daughter, and enjoys playing the drums.

artworks.description: A young woman rests closely against the head of a horse, their profiles merging into a single intimate composition. Built in pronounced relief, the work uses warm bronze and gold tones against a dark, textured ground, while turquoise details trace the woman’s hair, jewelry, and ornamentation. The sculptural surface gives the figures a weathered, almost archaeological quality, evoking tenderness, trust, and a deep connection between human and animal.

artworks.title: Fragments of Lascaux Cave

artist.name: Oksana Rubio

artworks.description: Inspired by the prehistoric imagery of the Lascaux caves, this textured composition evokes the fragmentary survival of ancient marks across time. A bull-like figure emerges from a layered, weathered surface of black, ochre, cream, and muted gold, surrounded by lines and forms that resemble eroded drawings, mineral stains, and traces of human touch. Structural paste gives the surface a rough, archaeological quality, making the work feel less like a depiction of cave art than a recovered section of an ancient wall.

image.alt: Fragments of Lascaux Cave by Oksana Rubio

artworks.description: A vibrant mass of sunflowers fills the canvas with color and movement. Brilliant yellows, fiery reds, deep greens, and flashes of turquoise create a dense, celebratory composition, while thick impasto gives the petals and leaves a lively sculptural presence. The dark flower centers are enriched with sparkling accents, adding depth and a shifting play of light across the surface. Energetic and abundant, the work captures the warmth, vitality, and exuberance of a garden at its peak.

artworks.title: Spring Petals

artist.name: Anastasia Ivasyuk
artist.bio:
My name is Anastasia Ivasyuk and I’m currently a student, about to go into my senior year of high school.
I don’t paint often but when I do, I enjoy making realism and impressionism pieces.

artworks.description: A honeybee rests against the center of a softly painted flower, its striped body and delicate wings rendered with greater detail than the surrounding bloom. Pale lavender petals spread across a calm blue background, creating a gentle contrast with the bee’s warm gold, brown, and black tones. The enlarged composition turns a familiar spring encounter into an intimate study of pollination, fragility, and seasonal renewal.

artworks.title: Tree of Life
artworks.description: A dense canopy of green unfolds across the canvas in layered, energetic brushstrokes. Twisting trunks and branches rise through the composition in warm browns, ochres, violet, and gold, while overlapping leaves create a shifting field of mint, turquoise, emerald, and yellow-green. Rather than describing a single tree literally, the painting captures the sensation of standing beneath living foliage—surrounded by movement, filtered light, and continual growth.

image.alt: Tree of Life by Paula Pokhodnya

artworks.title: Kyiv Sky
artworks.description: A broad summer sky opens above a lush garden landscape, where billowing clouds drift over dense trees, flowering fields, and glimpses of distant architecture. The foreground is alive with reds, pinks, blues, and yellow-greens, while the cooler city forms recede into the distance beneath an expansive blue sky. Painted with loose, expressive brushwork, the scene captures Kyiv as a place where cultivated beauty, urban memory, and nature meet.

artworks.title: Hollyhocks
artworks.description: A whitewashed cottage sits within a lush garden, framed by dense green foliage and a cluster of vivid hollyhocks near the doorway. Bright blue window frames, weathered rooflines, and scattered garden objects give the scene a lived-in, rural character. Loose, expressive brushwork and saturated color create the feeling of a warm summer day, where architecture and vegetation blend into a lively, intimate landscape.

artworks.description: A graceful arched bridge spans a still pond, framed by dense foliage in shifting greens, golds, and burgundy. Two figures pause at the center, introducing a quiet human presence into the landscape. Below, the bridge and surrounding trees dissolve into a richly colored reflection, doubling the scene and drawing the eye into the water’s depth. The work balances careful observation with expressive color, turning a garden setting into a contemplative study of light, symmetry, and connection.

artworks.title: Fall

artist.name: Ludmila Yuzhbabenko
artist.bio:
Ludmila Yuzhbabenko is an artist whose work celebrates the beauty of everyday life through expressive still lifes and evocative landscapes. 
Working primarily in oil and acrylic, she combines rich color, light, and texture to create paintings that invite viewers to pause and appreciate ordinary moments. Her subjects – from vibrant fruit compositions to tranquil natural scenes – reflect a deep appreciation for nature, memory, and the quite poetry found in familiar objects.

artworks.description: A quiet still life brings together late-season flowers and fruit in a balanced, carefully arranged composition. Deep purple, coral, and rose-colored blooms rise from a transparent glass vase, while grapes, an apple, and a pear rest across the tabletop below. The restrained background and soft modeling keep the focus on color, form, and the gentle abundance of autumn.

artworks.title: Taste of Home

artist.name: Viktoriia Useinova
artist.bio:
My name is Viktoriia Useinova. I am 31 years old, a mother of two, and originally from Kherson, Ukraine.

Creativity has always been an important part of my life. I have loved drawing and painting since childhood, attended art school, and later earned a university degree in Design.

Four years ago, because of the war in Ukraine, I moved to the United States, where I had to begin a new chapter of my life. Today, I work as a nail technician, but my love for art and the desire to create have always remained a part of who I am.

The painting presented in this exhibition is my first work after a long break and, in many ways, marks my return to painting. Through this piece, I wanted to capture a part of my memories, the warmth of home, and my connection to my hometown of Kherson.

artworks.description: A ripe watermelon and bright cut slices share the table with a vase of sunflowers, creating a still life filled with the colors and warmth of late summer. Cool blue-green tones surround the vivid red fruit and soft yellow petals, while scattered leaves and fallen blossoms give the arrangement a relaxed, lived-in quality. The familiar subjects evoke hospitality, harvest, and the simple comfort of food and flowers associated with home.

image.alt: Taste of Home by Viktoriia Useinova

artworks.title: Freedom

artist.name: Svitlana Ivasyuk
artist.bio:
Svitlana Ivasyuk (1974 -) is a Ukrainian American artist who lives and creates in Virginia Beach, Virginia. She was born and raised in Ukraine where rich national culture, mythology, and creativity were to shape and deeply influence her desire to create and bring beauty into everyday life, to develop and evolve as an artist, to be open and compassionate.
While having a formal education as a mathematician Svitlana is a self-taught artist. She creates in different styles including traditional Ukrainian decorative art of Petrykivka, watercolor, motanka doll making, macrame, beadwork, and neuro-art.
Her artworks have been exhibited at Las Laguna Art Gallery in California, Ukrainian American Archives and Museum in Michigan, San Diego Watercolor Society, and are owned by private art collectors all over the US and overseas as well. Recently her watercolor painting earned an Honorable Mention Award at SDWS.
Svitlana’s jewelry styles are very diverse. They are affected by history, by nature, and are deeply rooted in reflecting the inner world.  She loves to combine natural gemstones with modern beads from all over the world to create not only the visually beautiful piece but also a highly spiritual one that will connect with the essence of the owner.
Svitlana enjoys teaching others the magic of art, she conducts numerous workshops and private lessons in various painting styles and jewelry making.

artworks.description: A radiant abstract composition expands outward through interlocking organic forms and luminous color. Warm yellows and oranges gather around a dense central core of violet, blue, green, and rose, while fine black lines connect the shapes like a living network. The work suggests release, transformation, and energy in motion, balancing delicacy with a strong sense of emergence and freedom.

A small red-roofed pavilion anchors the rocky point while swimmers gather in the shallows and a cruise ship passes along the distant horizon. The scene captures the relaxed energy of Princess Cays, balancing vivid tropical color with the calm rhythm of sea, sand, and sky.

artworks.title: Apple Tree

artist.name: Margarita Pendiur
artist.bio:
Born in Kyiv, Ukraine, in 2002, I began my artistic journey at an early age. I graduated from an art school, where I received my first formal education in art. I was incredibly fortunate to learn from wonderful and inspiring teachers who had a profound influence on my artistic development. In 2022, I graduated from the Kyiv Academy of Arts, where I received a Bachelor’s degree in the field of Fine Arts, Decorative Art and Restoration, under the educational program Free Graphics, Design and Illustration of the Book. My professional qualification is Graphic Artist and Teacher.

Throughout my artistic journey, I have participated in more than 100 art competitions and exhibitions. Due to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, I was forced to temporarily relocate to the United States.

I currently focus mainly on oil painting, particularly in the landscape genre, while watercolor remains especially close to my heart. I enjoy experimenting with different techniques and artistic media.

Most of my paintings are inspired by nature — places that have left a lasting impression on me and deeply touched my soul. I believe that freedom and creativity are inseparable. In moments of silence, when I let go of accumulated knowledge and expectations, inspiration comes naturally, allowing something new and authentic to emerge.

artworks.description: A tangle of bare branches fills the composition, punctuated by dozens of bright yellow apples that glow against a cool blue-gray sky. The dense network of limbs creates an intricate, almost rhythmic pattern, while the remaining fruit brings warmth and vitality to the late-season landscape. The work captures a quiet moment of endurance, abundance, and beauty after the leaves have fallen.

artworks.description: A proud white rooster stands amid dense, weathered vegetation, its bright red comb cutting sharply through the muted greens and grays. Alert and steady, the bird becomes a symbol of resilience and defiance—rooted in its surroundings, unbowed, and unmistakably alive.

artworks.title: Sunflower Morning

artist.name: Svitlana Ivasyuk
artist.bio:
Svitlana Ivasyuk (1974 -) is a Ukrainian American artist who lives and creates in Virginia Beach, Virginia. She was born and raised in Ukraine where rich national culture, mythology, and creativity were to shape and deeply influence her desire to create and bring beauty into everyday life, to develop and evolve as an artist, to be open and compassionate.
While having a formal education as a mathematician Svitlana is a self-taught artist. She creates in different styles including traditional Ukrainian decorative art of Petrykivka, watercolor, motanka doll making, macrame, beadwork, and neuro-art.
Her artworks have been exhibited at Las Laguna Art Gallery in California, Ukrainian American Archives and Museum in Michigan, San Diego Watercolor Society, and are owned by private art collectors all over the US and overseas as well. Recently her watercolor painting earned an Honorable Mention Award at SDWS.
Svitlana’s jewelry styles are very diverse. They are affected by history, by nature, and are deeply rooted in reflecting the inner world.  She loves to combine natural gemstones with modern beads from all over the world to create not only the visually beautiful piece but also a highly spiritual one that will connect with the essence of the owner.
Svitlana enjoys teaching others the magic of art, she conducts numerous workshops and private lessons in various painting styles and jewelry making.

artworks.description: Bright sunflowers form the heart of this cheerful folk-inspired composition, surrounded by delicate blue blossoms, red berries, and richly patterned green leaves. Warm gold and orange tones create a sense of early light and optimism, while the balanced decorative arrangement celebrates abundance, renewal, and the simple joy of a new morning.

authors.name: Ludmila Yuzhbabenko
authors.bio:
Ludmila Yuzhbabenko is an artist whose work celebrates the beauty of everyday life through expressive still lifes and evocative landscapes. 
Working primarily in oil and acrylic, she combines rich color, light, and texture to create paintings that invite viewers to pause and appreciate ordinary moments. Her subjects – from vibrant fruit compositions to tranquil natural scenes – reflect a deep appreciation for nature, memory, and the quite poetry found in familiar objects.

authors.name: Oksana Rubio
authors.bio: Oksana Rubio is originally from Ukraine and teaches art at the Tidewater Ukrainian School in Virginia Beach. She enjoys working in the mediums of wood, paint, bas-relief, and textiles. Using her many talents, Oksana specializes in breathing fresh life into her art and furniture. Oksana is able to source unique items for Ancestral Energy through her many connections of friends and family around the globe. She currently lives in Suffolk with her husband and step-daughter, and enjoys playing the drums.

authors.name: Viktoriia Useinova
authors.bio:
My name is Viktoriia Useinova. I am 31 years old, a mother of two, and originally from Kherson, Ukraine.

Creativity has always been an important part of my life. I have loved drawing and painting since childhood, attended art school, and later earned a university degree in Design.

Four years ago, because of the war in Ukraine, I moved to the United States, where I had to begin a new chapter of my life. Today, I work as a nail technician, but my love for art and the desire to create have always remained a part of who I am.

The painting presented in this exhibition is my first work after a long break and, in many ways, marks my return to painting. Through this piece, I wanted to capture a part of my memories, the warmth of home, and my connection to my hometown of Kherson.

authors.name: Nataliia Sytnyk
authors.bio: Nataliia Sytnyk. Born 1974 in Ukraine in the city of Poltava.  Draws from childhood.  Graduated from Poltava Pedagogical University. Music and singing teacher. She is a professional artist and musician. She has had personal exhibitions in Ukraine, France and America. Many of her paintings are in private collections. Works with oil and acrylic. She loves to paint portraits and landscapes and adores Monet.
